title: Salman Khan Did a Cameo in an Egyptian Action Film. The Barber Shop Scene Went Viral Before the Movie Even Reached India.
excerpt: '7 Dogs' premiered in Egypt to massive crowds. Salman's poster dominated the venue. His English-language barber scene has already racked up millions of views. India release: May 28.
body:
Salman Khan doesn't need a full film to break the internet. Sometimes a barber shop scene is enough.

At the Egyptian premiere of *7 Dogs* — an international action thriller directed by Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah, the Belgian-Moroccan duo behind *Bad Boys for Life* and Marvel's *Ms. Marvel* — it wasn't the film's Egyptian leads who dominated the conversation. It was the massive Salman Khan posters plastered across the venue, and a viral clip of his cameo that's now racked up millions of views across social media.

The scene: Salman, seated in a barber's chair, delivering dialogue in English with the kind of effortless swagger that his fans have spent three decades rewarding with box office records. Fans immediately dubbed it a "paisa vasool entry" — high praise in Bollywood parlance, meaning you got your money's worth from a single moment.

## What Is '7 Dogs'?

The film stars Ahmed Ezz and Karim Abdel Aziz — two of Egypt's biggest actors — alongside Monica Bellucci and Sanjay Dutt. El Arbi and Fallah, who've become Hollywood's go-to action directors after the *Bad Boys* franchise, are making what's being described as a pan-regional action epic that bridges Middle Eastern, European, and South Asian star power.

Salman Khan's role is a cameo — brief but impactful enough that his poster at the Egyptian premiere was reportedly the most photographed element of the entire event. Sanjay Dutt also appears in what's described as a supporting cameo.

The film's trailer had already crossed 30 million views before the premiere, and the Egypt screening drew massive crowds. Salman did not attend the premiere in person, but his presence was felt through the footage that surfaced online within hours.

## Why This Matters Beyond the Cameo

There's something genuinely interesting happening here that goes beyond Salman Khan fan service.

*7 Dogs* represents a new model of international film production — one where star power is borrowed across borders to build a truly global audience. Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah understand this better than most: they're Belgian filmmakers of Moroccan descent who broke into Hollywood through *Bad Boys*, and now they're combining Egyptian, Indian, Italian, and Belgian talent in a single project.

For Salman Khan, this is a shrewd career move. His domestic box office has been inconsistent in recent years, but his brand value — especially in the Middle East, where Bollywood stars draw enormous audiences — remains immense. A cameo in *7 Dogs* costs him almost nothing in time and keeps him visible in markets that matter.

## The NRI Angle

For diaspora audiences, this is a cultural crossover moment worth paying attention to. Indian stars appearing in international productions is no longer novel — Priyanka Chopra, Deepika Padukone, and Ali Fazal have all done it. But Salman Khan in an Egyptian-Belgian action film is a different flavour of crossover. It's not about breaking into Hollywood. It's about the MENA-South Asia entertainment axis, where Bollywood's influence has always been strong but rarely formalised through co-productions.

The film hits Indian theatres on May 28. International release dates for the US, UK, and Canada haven't been formally announced, but given the co-production structure and Salman's global fanbase, worldwide prints are expected around the same window.

## What to Watch For

The real question is whether *7 Dogs* works as a film or merely as a collection of star cameos stitched into an action plot. El Arbi and Fallah have the craft to make the former happen — *Bad Boys for Life* was a genuinely good action film, not just a franchise exercise.

If the film delivers, it could open the door for more MENA-Indian co-productions — a market that's been underserved despite obvious audience overlap. If it doesn't, it'll still have given us a Salman Khan barber scene that'll circulate on WhatsApp family groups for the next decade.

Either way: May 28. Mark it.
nri_angle: This is the rare Indian star cameo in a genuine international production — directed by Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah (Bad Boys for Life, Ms. Marvel), with Monica Bellucci and top Egyptian stars. For NRIs, seeing Salman Khan in an Egyptian-Belgian action film is a cultural crossover moment. India release May 28, international dates TBA.
